task_summary: Define the interface contract for the Root component of the exemplar.tools documentation website. This root component orchestrates four child components (app_routing, page_components, project_scaffold, shared_components) and must establish the type system, re-exports, and integration surface that binds them together. The contract must align exactly with the canonical type registry and ensure all dependency contracts compose correctly at the root level.

findings.topic: Root component contract pattern for multi-component TypeScript projects
findings.finding: The root component in a decomposed frontend architecture should act as a thin composition layer — it imports from dependencies, wires them together, and re-exports the entry point. It should NOT redefine types owned by children; instead it re-exports them. The root's own contract surface is minimal: typically a bootstrap/render function and any top-level configuration types not owned elsewhere.
findings.source: TypeScript project architecture patterns (barrel exports, composition root)
findings.relevance: Directly defines what the root contract should contain: a render entry point, re-exported types from children, and integration wiring — nothing more.

findings.topic: Type re-export vs. redefinition in TypeScript barrel modules
findings.finding: Best practice is `export type { Foo } from './child'` rather than redefining Foo in the root. Redefinition causes drift and breaks structural typing guarantees when children update. The root barrel should use `export type` for type-only re-exports to enable proper tree-shaking and isolinear type flow.
findings.relevance: The canonical type registry assigns ownership to specific child components. Root must re-export, never redefine, these types.

findings.topic: Composition root wiring pattern for React + route manifest
findings.finding: The standard pattern: root imports getRouteManifest() from app_routing and getPageComponentMap() from page_components, composes them, and passes the result into App (from app_routing) which handles Router setup. The root is the only place where cross-cutting dependencies meet. This avoids circular dependencies between page_components and app_routing.
findings.source: React SPA architecture — dependency inversion at composition root
findings.relevance: Critical — the engineering decision explicitly states 'Page components depend on shared_components but not on app_routing'. Root is the integration seam.

findings.topic: PageComponentKey enum as string literal union vs. TypeScript enum
findings.finding: In modern TypeScript, prefer `type PageComponentKey = 'Home' | 'Cartographer' | ...` (string literal union) or `as const` object over `enum`. String literal unions are more composable, work better with Record<K,V>, and avoid the runtime overhead/quirks of TS enums. However, the canonical registry says 'enum' — the contract must match the registry's intent. If app_routing defines it as a TS enum, root must re-export that exact enum.
findings.source: TypeScript best practices — string unions vs enums; canonical type registry specification
findings.relevance: PageComponentKey is the primary discriminator connecting app_routing and page_components. The root must re-export the canonical form without alteration.

findings.topic: Entry point bootstrapping in Vite + React projects
findings.finding: The root entry point (main.tsx) calls renderEntryPoint() or ReactDOM.createRoot().render(<App />). In the dependency contract, app_routing exports renderEntryPoint. The root contract should expose a single bootstrapApplication() or simply re-export renderEntryPoint, plus ensure the App component receives its AppProps (which includes the PageComponentMap and RouteManifest).
findings.source: Vite React template conventions; app_routing dependency contract
findings.relevance: Defines the root's primary runtime function — the actual bootstrap call that wires everything together.

findings.finding: Root contract tests should verify: (1) all 13 PageComponentKey values have corresponding entries in both getRouteManifest() and getPageComponentMap(), (2) the composed App renders without throwing, (3) re-exported types are structurally compatible (compile-time check via type assertions in test files). Tests must not require a browser — use jsdom via vitest.
findings.relevance: The operating procedures mandate 'All functions must have at least one test' and 'No task is done until its contract tests pass'. Root tests verify integration correctness.

findings.topic: Avoiding circular dependencies in the component graph
findings.finding: The dependency graph is: root → {app_routing, page_components, project_scaffold, shared_components}; page_components → shared_components; app_routing → (receives PageComponentMap at runtime). The root must pass PageComponentMap into App/renderEntryPoint as a parameter — never should app_routing import from page_components directly. This inversion is the root's key architectural responsibility.
findings.source: Dependency inversion principle; engineering decision 'Page components depend on shared_components but not on app_routing'
findings.relevance: If the root contract doesn't make this dependency inversion explicit, implementers may introduce circular imports.

findings.topic: Project scaffold integration at root level
findings.finding: project_scaffold exports generateScaffold, getProjectManifest, getRequiredDependencies, validateScaffold. These are build-time/CI concerns, not runtime UI concerns. The root contract should re-export these for tooling consumers but they do not participate in the React render tree. Separating build-time from runtime exports prevents bundling scaffold logic into the client bundle.
findings.source: Build-time vs runtime separation patterns; project_scaffold dependency contract
findings.relevance: Ensures the root contract correctly categorizes scaffold functions as build/CI utilities, not UI wiring.

findings.topic: Named export requirements and default export pairing
findings.finding: Operating procedures mandate: every function/type/constant must be a named export. React components must have both named and default exports. The root module's main App wrapper (if any) must follow this pattern. Re-exports from children should preserve their export semantics.
findings.relevance: Non-negotiable project constraint that must be reflected in the root contract specification.

findings.topic: String key verification for route slugs and component maps
findings.finding: The operating procedures explicitly warn: 'NEVER infer key strings from component names or natural language — they may differ from the contract value.' Route slugs follow 'AS3 pattern exactly' per engineering decisions. The root contract tests must verify that route paths in the manifest match expected slug strings from the canonical source, not inferred from PageComponentKey variant names.
findings.source: Project operating procedures — String Keys in Maps and Registries
findings.relevance: Critical pitfall. Route path '/constrain' vs '/constraint', '/kindex' vs '/k-index' — these must come from the contract, not guessed.

recommended_approach:
The Root contract should be a thin composition layer with the following surface:

**Types (all re-exported from children, never redefined):**
- Re-export all canonical types from app_routing: PageComponentKey, RouteEntry, RouteManifest, RoutePath, RouteLabel, PageComponentMap, ReactComponentType, AppProps
- Re-export all canonical types from shared_components: CalloutType, CalloutBoxProps, CodeBlockProps, VersionBadgeProps, VideoEmbedProps, SidebarProps, PageLayoutProps, ReactNode
- Re-export scaffold types from project_scaffold: ProjectManifest, DependencyEntry, ScaffoldResult, etc.

**Functions (root-owned):**
1. `bootstrapApp(): void` — the main composition function that:
   - Calls `getRouteManifest()` from app_routing
   - Calls `getPageComponentMap()` from page_components
   - Passes both into `renderEntryPoint()` from app_routing
2. Re-export all child functions for consumer convenience (barrel pattern)

**Root-specific types (if any):**
- `BootstrapConfig` — optional configuration for the bootstrap function (e.g., target DOM element ID)

**Contract tests must verify:**
1. `getRouteManifest()` returns exactly 13 entries
2. `getPageComponentMap()` returns a map with exactly the 13 PageComponentKey values
3. Every key in the route manifest has a corresponding entry in the page component map (bijection)
4. `bootstrapApp()` can be called without throwing (jsdom)
5. Type compatibility assertions (compile-time)

**Key architectural constraint to encode:** The root is the ONLY place where app_routing and page_components meet. The PageComponentMap is injected into App/renderEntryPoint as a parameter — this dependency inversion must be explicit in the contract.
alternatives_considered: Root defines its own wrapper App component that imports from all children — rejected because app_routing already owns the App component; root should compose, not wrap.
Root re-defines canonical types locally for 'convenience' — rejected because it violates the type registry ownership model and risks drift.
Root imports page_components lazily via React.lazy for code splitting — viable optimization but premature for the contract definition phase; can be added later without changing the contract surface.

Merge project_scaffold exports into the same entry point as runtime UI — rejected because it would bundle build-time utilities into the client; prefer separate entry points or tree-shaking-friendly re-exports.
Use a single default export object containing all wired dependencies — rejected per operating procedures requiring named exports.
risks: Route slug mismatch: If root tests don't verify exact path strings from the canonical source, slug drift between app_routing and page_components will cause runtime 404s. Mitigate by testing the bijection between manifest paths and component keys.

Circular dependency: If app_routing ever imports from page_components directly (bypassing root injection), the build will either fail or produce undefined values. Mitigate by encoding the injection pattern in the contract and testing it.
Type redefinition drift: If root redefines any canonical type instead of re-exporting, changes in the owning child won't propagate. Mitigate by using `export type { X } from './child'` exclusively.

Bundle bloat from project_scaffold: Scaffold utilities include Node.js-specific code (file generation, validation) that shouldn't be in the browser bundle. Mitigate by separating scaffold re-exports into a distinct entry point or ensuring tree-shaking eliminates them.

Missing PageComponentKey variant: If a new page is added to the enum but not to the component map or route manifest, the app will crash at runtime. Mitigate with exhaustiveness checks in the contract test (verify all 13 keys present in both structures).

import.meta.env misuse: Per operating procedures, any env access must use `import.meta.env.VITE_X` directly — never cast through `as any`. Root bootstrap may need env vars (e.g., VITE_CONVEX_URL); must follow the prescribed pattern.
compliance_notes: All output files must be .ts/.tsx — no Python generation permitted.
Named exports required on all types, interfaces, functions, constants. React components must pair named + default exports.
Every .tsx file must include `import React from 'react'` at the top.
Tests use vitest + @testing-library/react in jsdom environment.
Type annotations required on all public functions.
All functions must have at least one test; tests must run without external services.
String keys in maps must be verified against the canonical source of truth (type registry, contract test data, or dependency manifests) — never inferred from names.
import.meta.env must be accessed directly, never via `(import.meta as any).env?.`.
Canonical types from the registry must be re-exported exactly as defined — never redefined with different fields.
